scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-AI-AUTOFIX-RESOLVES-ROOT-CAU.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a response-handling gap, solvable by an AI agent that auto-answers tickets and automatically fixes whatever is producing wrong bills.

H-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August caused reads to be rejected or misclassified, triggering erroneous estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-AMI-EXPORT-FAILURE.statement: The AMI vendor's nightly MDMS export to billing (H-MDMS-BILL) degraded or failed starting around August, causing missing/incorrect interval reads and forced estimate substitution.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: The contracted manual meter-reading process (H-FIELD-BILL) degraded since August — e.g. incomplete routes or staffing shortfalls — producing late/incorrect manual reads and wrong bills.

H-DISPUTE-PERCEPTION-NOT-BILL.statement: Bills are substantively correct; the ticket-volume doubling reflects a CRM/process artifact (e.g., duplicate tickets, slower response causing re-contacts) rather than an actual increase in billing error rate.

interpretation_history.interpretation: A billing-db query for logged tariff/rate changes during the dispute period returned zero records, ruling out a rate/tariff change as a direct cause of the bill disputes within the window examined. This is a negative finding that narrows the search space but does not bear on any of the currently listed causal hypotheses, none of which invoke tariff changes.

Of 3025 disputed bills, 1785 (59%) were based on ACTUAL meter reads and 1240 (41%) on ESTIMATED reads. The majority of disputes are tied to bills with real (non-estimated) reads, which read-type-substitution hypotheses (AMI export failure, rule change) would not predict as the dominant pattern.

CRM monthly dispute counts show a ~600/month baseline in June-July 2026 (610, 590) rising to 1180 in August and 1260 in September — confirming a real near-doubling of ticket volume coincident with the claimed surge. The data only establishes the magnitude/timing of the volume increase; it says nothing about what is causing the underlying bills to be disputed.

CRM response-time data covering 2440 tickets (matching E-03's Aug+Sep count of 1180+1260) shows median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days, both inside the 3.0-day SLA, so ticket response speed is not currently a performance gap. This undercuts the framing that the surge is primarily a slow-response/handling problem requiring an AI auto-responder.

Route-log data for the Aug-Sep dispute window shows field manual-meter-read route completion at 88% against a 95% target across 9200 manual-read accounts, i.e. a real ~7-point shortfall in the contracted field-reading process during the surge period. This is consistent with incomplete/late manual reads but does not by itself establish that these incomplete routes are what produced the disputed bills.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states there was no tariff change this year, which agrees with the tool-derived finding E-01 (zero tariff_change_log records) on the same question. As a stakeholder statement it is non-authoritative and adds no new causal information beyond corroborating E-01.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD attributes the Aug-Sep route completion shortfall (already shown as fact in E-05) to a reader staffing gap since July, offering a candidate mechanism linking understaffing to late routes and estimated-bill substitution. This is an unverified, non-authoritative stakeholder claim from someone whose incentives favor a staffing narrative (contract headcount increase), not independent confirmation of root cause.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract clause confirms that route priority changes requested by the utility must be executed only after Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) confirmation, formalizing the authorization/approval pathway for the push_route_update protected action already reflected in constraint K-DISPATCH.
